title: Reaction mechanisms
examples: How do I draw the arrows for this reaction?
What is the difference between electrophilic and nucleophilic reactions?
Can you show me an example of an SN2 reaction?

explain.say: Today we will look at reaction mechanisms in organic chemistry. We use curly arrows to show electron movement during reactions.

items: They start at a source and end at a destination.
They always show pairs of electrons moving.

explain.say: Electrophilic addition happens when an electron-poor molecule reacts with an electrophile. Think of adding across a double bond.
Nucleophilic substitution involves a nucleophile replacing a leaving group on a carbon atom. The nucleophile attacks the carbon.
A common example is the addition of bromine to an alkene. The bromine electrophile adds across the pi bond.
Another example is the reaction of an alkyl halide with hydroxide. The hydroxide is the nucleophile replacing the halide.
In real life, when you treat an unsaturation with water, it undergoes electrophilic addition. This forms an alcohol.

draw.text: Real Life: Water Adding to Unsaturated Bonds

faq.q: What is the difference between an electrophile and a nucleophile?
faq.a: An electrophile is electron-poor and seeks electrons. A nucleophile is electron-rich and donates electrons.
asks: Which species attacks the electron cloud?

faq.q: Do all substitution reactions use curly arrows?
faq.a: Yes, drawing the mechanism requires showing the movement of electron pairs with curly arrows.
asks: How do I show the electron movement?

faq.q: Is the reaction mechanism always the same for an alkene?
faq.a: No, the specific electrophile or nucleophile changes the exact steps and intermediates formed.
asks: Does the reactant determine the mechanism?
Can I change the product by changing the reagent?

faq.q: What is the role of the leaving group in substitution?
faq.a: The leaving group is the atom or group that departs with the electrons, taking the bonding pair with it.
asks: Why does the leaving group leave?
Does the leaving group need to be stable?

faq.q: When is electrophilic addition favored over substitution?
faq.a: Electrophilic addition is favored when a pi bond, like in an alkene, is present and highly reactive.
asks: Does the presence of a double bond change things?
Which reaction type is best for unsaturation?

facts: Electrophiles are electron deficient species, often bearing a positive charge.
Nucleophiles are electron rich species, often bearing a negative charge.
Curly arrows must always start at an electron source and point to an electron sink.
In substitution, the nucleophile attacks the carbon bearing the leaving group.

quiz.say: If a molecule has a double bond, which type of reaction is most likely to occur?
quiz.why: The double bond makes the carbons electron-rich and susceptible to attack by electrophiles.

wrong.0: This mechanism involves unpaired electrons, not the movement of pairs shown by arrows.
wrong.1: Elimination removes groups, whereas addition adds groups across the bond.
wrong.3: This usually requires a good leaving group attached to a saturated carbon.

quiz.say: In an SN2 reaction, what must the nucleophile do to the carbon bearing the leaving group?

options.show: Attack only on the leaving group
options.say: Attack only on the leaving group

options.show: Attack only after the leaving group departs
options.say: Attack only after the leaving group departs

quiz.why: The backside attack minimizes steric hindrance and is characteristic of the SN2 mechanism.

wrong.1: Frontside attack is often associated with carbocation intermediates.
wrong.2: The nucleophile must attack the carbon atom itself.
wrong.3: The attack and departure happen in one concerted step for SN2.

quiz.say: When drawing the mechanism for bromine adding to ethene, which arrow correctly shows the first step?

options.show: Arrow from pi bond to Br molecule
options.say: Arrow from pi bond to Br molecule

options.show: Arrow from one C-H bond to Br
options.say: Arrow from one C-H bond to Br

options.show: Arrow from Br to the pi bond
options.say: Arrow from Br to the pi bond

quiz.why: The pi bond acts as the electron source, attacking the electrophilic bromine molecule.

wrong.1: The pi bond is the most electron-rich site available for the initial attack.
wrong.2: The bromine molecule is the electrophile and accepts the electron pair.
wrong.3: A reaction mechanism must show the movement of electrons using arrows.
